attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, restating his earlier WeWork analogy.

semantics.note: 'I think' states a belief but carries no graded hedge such as 'I suspect' or 'may'. It is a forecast with no deadline. 'Someday' and 'drawing close' are kept as qualifiers.

contract.note: Reading 'WeWork of AI' as a business collapse after heavy financing is a fair, ordinary reading of the context ('toast', 'just before it fell'). The contract correctly sets no deadline and treats continued operation as non-conclusive.

evidence.note: SoftBank says it completed its $30B follow-on investment on 2026-10-01. This weighs against imminence, but it is a company disclosure and cannot settle an undated forecast.

reviews.rationale: No deadline was stated, and the packet has no qualifying bankruptcy, distress restructuring or valuation collapse. Continued financing through October 2026 cuts against 'drawing close', but by the contract's terms it cannot contradict 'someday'. The forecast stays open.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: The factual core is that Nvidia pulled back on its $100B pledge in the prior week. 'Terrible signal' is correctly set aside as evaluation.

contract.note: Requiring a material retreat from the overall staged plan is a fair reading. The strict Feb 2–8 window is somewhat narrow for casual 'last week' wording, and the result partly depends on it.

evidence.note: The Sept 2025 announcement sets the baseline: an intent to invest up to $100B progressively. It predates the target week.

Huang said on Feb 3 that the plans remained on track. That is the company's own denial. The same report notes a ~$20B round contribution and a WSJ report that the plan had stalled. The signals are mixed and settle nothing.

reviews.rationale: The packet does not establish a material reduction of Nvidia's overall $100B intention in the target week. Huang's denial is a corporate statement, which the contract says cannot settle disputed private negotiations. The $20B round report does not show the overall ceiling was cut. The evidence settles neither side.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: This faithfully restates a present-tense competitive-landscape observation as of Feb 2026.

contract.note: Reading this as frontier capability, with 'largely' meaning broadly competitive and at least two Chinese developers improving, is a fair, ordinary plain reading.

evidence.note: The Jan 20, 2026 v1 of APEX-Agents puts Gemini 3 Flash ahead of GPT-5.2 on agentic professional tasks.
Artificial Analysis (Feb 6) puts Opus 4.6 first on its Intelligence Index, ahead of GPT-5.2. The later sidebar on the page is ignored.
Artificial Analysis (Jan 27) says Moonshot's Kimi K2.5 is closer than ever to the frontier.
Artificial Analysis (Feb 11) shows Z.AI's GLM-5 up 8 index points and calls it a significant narrowing of the gap.

reviews.rationale: Independent, contemporaneous evaluations put a Google model and an Anthropic model at or above OpenAI on important measures. Two separate Chinese developers (Moonshot and Z.AI) show measured progress toward the frontier. This meets the contract's support condition, though not full parity on every task.
